problem_type: CI job display name misrepresents what the job actually runs
symptom: The quality-gate workflow job labelled "Desktop Linux" runs Electron smoke, CI-safe user journeys, critical and full canvas acceptance, and the canvas performance budget under xvfb, then uploads walkthrough screenshots and output.jsonl — i.e. it is the Linux end-to-end walkthrough lane, not a generic "desktop" build. The label read as a platform/build stage and hid that a red here is a user-journey/walkthrough failure.
direct_cause: When the quality gate was parallelized into Ubuntu jobs (docs/superpowers/plans/2026-08-28-quality-gate-parallel-orchestration.md), the end-to-end lane inherited the generic name "Desktop Linux" instead of naming the behavior it verifies.
class_root: A CI job's display name is free text with no contract tying it to the steps it runs, so a name can drift from behavior without any signal. This is the CI-surface sibling of the architecture audit's broader finding that names (dead code, stale job labels) diverge from what code does.
affected_population: Maintainers reading a failed Quality Gate run who must guess whether "Desktop Linux" failed on a build, a smoke test, or a canvas walkthrough
Anyone triaging CI who relies on the job label to jump to the right evidence artifact (linux-walkthrough-evidence)
entry_points: GitHub Actions run summary job list (the label shown next to each job)
CI annotation hygiene collector, which surfaces per-job names in its output
invariants: The Linux end-to-end lane is named for the behavior it verifies (E2E walkthroughs), not for a platform build stage.
The job id remains desktop-linux, so branch protection and the require-all Quality Gate job (which reference the id, not the display name) are unaffected.
Branch protection required status checks stay Quality Gate and Mac Package; no protection context references the renamed display name.
residual_risks: Job display names are still free text with no gate asserting name-to-behavior fidelity; a future job could again be misnamed. This is accepted as low blast-radius (a label, not executable behavior) and out of scope for this cosmetic rename.
The renamed lane runs more than walkthroughs (smoke + journeys + canvas acceptance + performance); "E2E Walkthroughs (Linux)" is a best-effort umbrella, not an exhaustive enumeration.

recurrence.reason: This is a single mislabeled job corrected to match its steps, not a defect class that regenerates. There is no code path that manufactures job names, so no structural prevention is warranted; inventing a name-fidelity gate would be over-engineering for a display-string change.
same_class_scan: Grepped the repository for the literal string "Desktop Linux": the only production reference was .github/workflows/quality-gate.yml (the job name) plus two mock fixtures in scripts/ci-annotation-hygiene.node-test.mjs; the remaining hits are immutable historical plan/spec records that describe the past state and are intentionally left unchanged.
Confirmed no other quality-gate.yml job label misrepresents its steps: Contracts, Unit, Mac Package, and Quality Gate each name what they run.

Verified via gh api that branch protection required status checks reference only "Quality Gate" and "Mac Package", and that both the require-all job and the workflow structure tests reference the desktop-linux job id (not its display name), so the rename cannot silently drop a required check.

internal_only_reason: This is an internal CI job-label correction; there is no external API or third-party documentation contract involved. The relevant facts (job steps, job id vs display name, branch protection contexts) were verified directly against the repository workflow and the live GitHub branch-protection API.

legacy_paths.rationale: No parallel or legacy path is introduced or removed; the job id and its steps are unchanged and only the human-readable display name is corrected.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: A CI display-name correction involves no dependency version or runtime lifecycle change.

migration: The job id desktop-linux is unchanged, so no downstream reference (branch protection, needs graph, workflow structure tests) requires migration. Only the display name changes from "Desktop Linux" to "E2E Walkthroughs (Linux)"; the two ci-annotation-hygiene mock fixtures are updated to the new name so the sample data stays representative.
